title: test(plugin-sharing): bring the two share-link password test files under the 10 s budget
body:
Refs #23184 (plugin-sharing rows)
Clause-②: no — test wall time only; no published schema, behaviour or export moves.

A partial landing of the `domain:services` test-budget card. This PR answers only the two `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` rows. The other packages' rows (plugin-auth, plugin-security, service-datasource, organizations) are not addressed here, and #23184 remains open for them.

## Rows this PR answers

| file | card reading (hourly full battery) | before, median of 3 | after, median of 3 |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| `src/share-link-password.test.ts` | 38.2 s | 11.90 s | **1.18 s** |
| `src/share-link-password-webcontainer.test.ts` | 10.9 s | 2.84 s | **2.04 s** |

Tests only: no production file, option or export changes. Every case and every expectation from before is still there (proof below).

## What the files were waiting on (measured)

- **H1 holds: scrypt at the production parameters (N=16384, r=16), nothing else.** A temporary probe that counted `node:crypto.scrypt` calls per case found **96 native derivations across the main file's 44 cases**, about 0.115 s each on this box. Most of them did work the file had already done. They derived the same password against the same salt again, minted a hash only so a later route case could verify the right password against it, or (in 4 legacy cases) minted a placeholder password's hash that was overwritten before anything read it. Per case, boot and routing cost about 10-15 ms.
- **H2: a seam exists but is not used.** The service's injectable hasher pair (`hashPassword` / `verifyPassword`) exists, but injecting it switches off the legacy re-hash path. That behaviour is pinned ("is not attempted when the deployment injects its own hasher pair"), so these files keep the default hasher and production code is untouched. No new option or export was needed, so `Clause-②` stays `no`.
- **H3: the WebContainer file waits on no timer and no container boot.** Its 4 cases ran 9 pure-JS plus 9 native derivations at the production parameters. The pure-JS derivation (`@noble/hashes`) costs about twice the native one.

## What changed

`share-link-password.test.ts`
1. **A per-file `node:crypto.scrypt` memo** keyed by every input: password, salt, key length and cost parameters. scrypt is a pure function, so a hit answers with the bytes a fresh call would produce. A verifier that derived with another normalisation, salt or parameter would miss the memo and run the real derivation. Concurrent requests for one input wait on the derivation already in flight. Nothing above `node:crypto` is replaced, so `share-link-password.ts` parses, dispatches, compares and refuses as in production.
2. **Cases about what happens after minting share one real hash per password per file.** This covers routes, encodings, cache headers, the list and redemption exits, and the verifier. The hash comes from `fixtureHash`, which is the real `hashShareLinkPassword`. It is seeded onto a link minted without a password, the same way the legacy cases already seed theirs. Three cases still mint through the service with the password: the two about minting itself (the mint response, the per-row salt) and the no-log case, whose logger scope includes the mint.
3. **The legacy cases mint with no password.** Before, they minted with a placeholder password whose scrypt hash was overwritten before any read.
4. **Cases run concurrently.** Every case boots its own engine, service, routes and logger, so each top-level suite is `describe.concurrent`. Engines are now destroyed in `afterAll` instead of `afterEach`, which would destroy an engine a running case still holds. The concurrency is what overlaps the derivations that cannot be shared (minting and re-hashing under fresh salts) on the libuv pool. A probe confirmed the one case that edits an object's sharing policy edits only its own engine's copy of the schema: a second engine does not see the edit. Case names are unchanged: there is no wrapper suite.

`share-link-password-webcontainer.test.ts`
1. **One memo per implementation** (native `node:crypto.scrypt`, pure-JS `scryptAsync`). The two are never shared, so every cross-implementation check is still a real derivation on the other path. Probe per case, real and memo-answered derivations on each path: `beforeAll` 1/0, case 1 1/0, case 2 2/0, case 3 3/1, case 4 0/0, identical on both paths. The only memo hits are the NFKC case's second spelling, whose normalised input the first spelling already derived. A path that skipped NFKC would miss the memo.
2. **PASSWORD's hash is minted once per path, in `beforeAll`.** The cross-verify case and the byte-identity case share it. One assertion is added there: only the native mint may reach `node:crypto.scrypt`. If the shared "pure-JS" hash was not really minted by the pure-JS path, the hook fails.

**Budgets:** no timeout is raised or lowered. The three explicit budgets keep their values. Their comments now give the new derivation counts and say each budget stands until a `Test Core` reading of the new shape re-sizes it.

## Proof

**Wall time.** The reading is vitest's own per-file duration: the JSON reporter's `endTime - startTime`, the same figure the module line prints and the hourly captures parse. Every run used the same command, ran each file alone in `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing` under the shared verify lock, three runs each:

`pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 FILE --reporter=verbose --reporter=json --outputFile.json=OUT`

| file | before @ `4cc3ff9dc6` (ms) | median | after @ `055d9304cc` (ms) | median | ratio |
|:--|:--|--:|:--|--:|--:|
| `share-link-password.test.ts` | 11224 / 12522 / 11904 | 11904 | 1176 / 1110 / 1212 | 1176 | 10.1x |
| `share-link-password-webcontainer.test.ts` | 3035 / 2841 / 2739 | 2841 | 2037 / 2172 / 1944 | 2037 | 1.39x |

This container is shared with other agents, so these absolute numbers are readings from a shared box; the ratios are the robust part.

**CI projection.** I read the `test-core-timings` captures from five recent hourly full-battery runs (`38294929860`, `38354632561`, `38361439350`, `38366978022`, `38373927133`):

- Main file: 38.2 / 34.0 / 41.5 / 37.9 / 38.1 s, i.e. 2.9-3.5x this box's before-median.
- WebContainer file: 9.2 / 7.0 / 8.5 / 9.8 / 10.5 s, i.e. 2.5-3.7x.

At the worst of those ratios, the after-medians project to about **4.1 s** and **7.5 s**. The WebContainer file's floor is 7 pure-JS plus 8 native production-parameter derivations, and every one of them is something a case is about. The card's pin, "the next refresh PR's list no longer names the file", is the measurement that decides this.

**Same cases, same expectations.** No ablation is owed for a speed-only change; the evidence is the case lists and the `expect` lines.

- Case names and statuses (sorted `fullName` plus status), before run 1 compared with each of the six after-runs: identical every time, 44/44 and 4/4 passed.
- Every `expect` line in both files is byte-identical between base and head (sorted line diff of the files). The one added line is the WebContainer `beforeAll` guard above. `expect(` counts: main file 78 before, 78 after; WebContainer file 20 before, 21 after.

## Local verification (head `055d9304cc`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-sharing run typecheck`: green. Both files are in `tsconfig.test.json`'s program (`--listFilesOnly`) and add nothing to `test-typecheck-debt.json`.
- The whole package, `vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 42 files, 1025 tests passed, on the tree merged with `origin/main` (the closure rebuilt first, because main moved `packages/objectql`).
- ESLint, narrowed to this diff's 2 files (`--no-inline-config --format json`): 2 files linted, 0 errors, 0 warnings. Neither file is ignored, so the population is exactly this diff. `eslint.config.mjs` never enables type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project` anywhere), so these files cannot change a verdict on an untouched file. The full `pnpm lint` runs in CI.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` (no paths; change set = these 2 files against the merge base `01a3421f4`) derived 54 commands, the same list as the dispatch's reading.
  - All 54 exit 0 at `055d9304cc`. Each ran separately, with its exit code captured before any pipe.
  - `dispatch-gates --ran` reconciliation: 54 derived, 54 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN. That zero is derived from the recorded exit codes, none of which is 3.
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n` answered PREREQUISITE NOT MET (exit 3) on a first sweep, before the workspace was built. After a full `turbo run build`, both measured and passed.
  - Not run locally: the rows the derivation lists outside its 54 (the path-scheduled Test Core, Build Core and dogfood jobs, the type-check lanes, the artifact-roster families). Those belong to CI.

## Acceptance notes

- The main file spends about 18 s of import and transform time on this box (vitest `import 17.7-19.2 s`, `transform 14.5-15.8 s`, both before and after; the cause was not measured). That time is outside the per-file reading this budget grades. It is noted here only; it is not a finding.
- No `Test Core` reading exists yet for the new shapes. The explicit budgets stay as sized until one does.

## Changeset

None. The diff is tests only, and `files` ships `dist`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`, so no test file is published. `skip-changeset` applies.
